note: WHY THIS CYCLE EXISTS. The first Gate 4 apply today accepted 164 pages generated BEFORE the prose-rejoin work, so the accepted manual carried sentences broken mid-clause. This cycle projects command-reference candidate MANRUN-20260902T154553Z-14F5CEEE, the first candidate in which all three properties hold at once: PART_NO spills reassembled (canary reads 'not the command name.', cdx reads '(AIF-043).', sql reads 'does not mutate table data.'), lists left intact (model.md keeps '- tables' and '- records' as separate bullets; buffering.md keeps '- working state' and '- persisted state'), and none of the six corrupted or welded forms present anywhere across the 164 pages.
superseded_plan_note: THREE earlier plans for this cycle were built and NOT applied, each discarded on review rather than on a gate: MANRUN-20260902T153114Z-472B26D9 and MANRUN-20260902T153842Z-CBC1CCB6 (and the candidates behind them). Two distinct defects, both invisible to the fragment count that was supposed to measure this work. (1) CORRUPTION: a length heuristic joined 240-byte spills with a space, turning 'not the command name.' into 'not the comm and name.' and '(AIF-043).' into '(AIF-04 3).'. (2) WELDING: with no minimum length, wrapped-prose joining fused list items -- model.md tables/records/fields, expression.md numeric/character/date, script.md loops, buffering.md working/persisted state, about thirty items across eight pages. Both were caught by diffing staged pages against accepted ones and requiring every difference to be explained; neither would have been caught by counting fragments, because a wrong join lowers that count exactly like a right one.
ledger_hash_note: The status ledger hash is byte-identical to the values approved on 2026-07-28 (MANRUN-20260728T034317Z-BB9D66A2) and earlier today (MANRUN-20260902T130837Z-AFAAC0E3). That is EXPECTED and is not a copied value: all three runs report zero status dispositions, so all three ledgers are the same 29-byte header-only artifact ('status,note' / 'EMPTY,No rows.'). It was recomputed with sha256 from status_disposition_ledger.csv on disk for THIS run and matched, rather than carried forward from either earlier record. A hash that repeats because the input is genuinely identical is evidence; a hash that repeats because nobody recomputed it is the AIF-118 shape, and the two are indistinguishable from the file alone -- hence this note.
mechanism_note: The spill fix is no longer a heuristic. src/help/helpdata_export_dbf.cpp documents HELP_LINE as a deliberate pseudo-memo -- 'one logical line is split into 240-byte PARTS across numbered rows, and the reader reassembles by LINE_NO + PART_NO' -- under a heading that says DO NOT 'FIX' IT. The renderer now uses that key. The measurements derived by hand during this run (6 rows at exactly 240; PART_NO 1/2/3 = 29693/6/1) are printed in that same comment, measured 2026-08-25, which also predicted the misreading: 'An agent reading LINE_NO / PART_NO / TEXT(240) cold reads it as an implementation quirk -- one did.' The owner's question, 'do we have a simple problem of needing longer fields?', is what sent this session to the producer. The answer is no: the field is not too short, and the reassembly key already existed.
